glosses: To start moving.

examples.text: Driver Cerr spent so long complaining to us about the quality of the coal that we had barely time to get into coach No. 51, the oldest type of third-class six-wheeler, as we moved off.

glosses: Used other than figuratively or idiomatically: see move, away.
To go away from a place, especially when permanently changing one's residence.

examples.text: I lost contact with my friend after she had moved away.

By Tuesday evening the track had been cleared to the three snowbound engines, and the following day, under their own steam, they were moved away; the business of relighting their fires and raising steam in such conditions is better imagined than described.

translations.source_sense_description: перемещаться, увеличивая своё расстояние от кого-либо, чего-либо

glosses: To fit (a vehicle) with new tires.
To stop working on a permanent basis, usually because of old age or illness.

examples.text: Having made a large fortune, he retired.
He wants to retire at 55.
She decided to retire from her banking job due to stress.
Green will never forget "that was the day I retired - the absolute crowning event of my life and I was very proud of that.

glosses: To stop playing their sport and in competitions a sports player.

examples.text: I have decided to retire from test cricket at 45.
I have decided to retire from football at the end of the season after the World Cup.

glosses: To withdraw; to take away.

examples.text: He […] retired himself, his wife, and children into a forest.
As when the sun is present all the year, / And never doth retire his golden ray.

glosses: To cease use or production of something.

examples.text: The steamship made thousands of trips over several decades before it was retired by the shipping company.
When a hurricane becomes so deadly or destructive that future use would be insensitive, officials may retire the name of the hurricane.
Only now, due to the COVID-19-associated drop in traffic, are they being retired with 12 of the 30 trains moved to Landore (Swansea) for warm storage.

glosses: To withdraw from circulation, or from the market; to take up and pay.

examples.text: The central bank retired those notes five years ago.

glosses: To cause to retire; specifically, to designate as no longer qualified for active service; to place on the retired list.

examples.text: The board retired the old major.

How had it felt, at 28, to be the hottest young actor in town? He [Richard Gere] grinned. “It was great having the attention,” he said. “I thought: ‘This is it! I’ve done it! I’m going to retire my father. I’m putting money away for college for my sisters,’ the whole thing. It’s incredibly euphorious. All of a sudden the rehearsal period of your life is over, and your future has arrived. It’s liberating.”

By the time I first spoke to Magana in late 2022, 25/7 Media’s success had given him some measure of financial security. “The truth is that I just retired my parents,” he told me two days after Christmas.

glosses: To voluntarily stop batting before being dismissed so that the next batsman can bat.

examples.text: Jones retired in favour of Smith.

glosses: To make a play which results in a runner or the batter being out, either by means of a put out, fly out or strikeout. Also, when such an event ends a team's turn at bat.

examples.text: Jones retired Smith 6-3.
Jones makes the catch for the third out, and that retires the side.

glosses: To go back or return; to withdraw or retreat, especially from public view; to go into privacy.

examples.text: I will retire to the study.
to retire from the world
to retire from the public eye

glosses: To retreat from action or danger; to withdraw for safety or pleasure.

examples.text: to retire from battle
The regiment retired from the fray after the Major was killed.

glosses: To recede; to fall or bend back.

examples.text: Past the point, the shore retires into a sequence of coves.

glosses: To go to bed.

examples.text: I will retire for the night.

In the daytime the beds are made up but completely out of sight, giving the passenger a comfortable little private room; as the time for retiring comes, after preparing for rest in the same spacious conditions, he is able, practically at a touch, to pull the bed into position ready for use.

glosses: The act of retiring, or the state of being retired.
A place to which one retires.
A call sounded on a bugle, announcing to skirmishers that they are to retire, or fall back.

examples.text: At the retire, the cavalry fell back.

glosses: To draw or pull (something) away or back from its original position or situation.

examples.text: One [poem] by Hercules Rollock on the marriage of Anne of Denmark is better, and equal, a few names withdrawn, to any of the contemporaneous poetry of France.
